"Sundhedsklynge" (Health Cluster) refers to the regional organizational framework in Denmark used to group municipalities for the purpose of coordinating health services [^src1]. This structure plays a critical role in the national healthcare system, particularly when analyzing regional variations in patient populations and healthcare professional capacity, such as the distribution of practicing cardiologists [^src1]. 

In the context of the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) report on atrial fibrillation in Denmark, health clusters are utilized as a geographic and administrative unit to measure and improve the quality of clinical treatment for chronic heart diseases [^src1]. The data serves as an evidence base for political and clinical decisions regarding resource allocation and treatment standards across the country's regions [^src1]. 

Specific municipalities identified within these health clusters include [[bornholm|Bornholm]], which operates as its own cluster ("Sundhedsklynge Bornholm"), as well as the City of [[koebenhavn|København]] and the City of [[frederiksberg|Frederiksberg]], which are designated as "Sundhedsklynge Byen København" and "Sundhedsklynge Byen Frederiksberg," respectively [^src1]. Beyond these specific municipal groupings and their mention on page 93 of the RKKP report, no further detailed claims or chronological events are available in the current dataset.
